title: CHF Discharge Protocol - HealthFirst
content: Reduce 30-day CHF readmissions by completing medication reconciliation, low-sodium diet education, daily weight instructions, and follow-up within 7 days. High-risk criteria include prior admission, CKD stage 3+, living alone, and polypharmacy. Perform phone outreach within 48 hours and escalate with dyspnea, edema, or rapid weight gain.

title: Sepsis Early Warning and Escalation Workflow
content: Escalate when two or more trigger conditions are present: abnormal temperature, heart rate > 90, respiratory rate > 20, and suspected infection. Complete 60-minute bundle with blood cultures, lactate, antibiotics, and fluids. Escalate to ICU consult for persistent hypotension or elevated lactate.

title: Emergency Department Triage Policy
content: Define triage levels 1 through 5 with throughput targets of door-to-triage <= 10 minutes and door-to-provider <= 30 minutes for level 2 and 3. Flag frequent flyers with 4+ ED visits in 12 months for care coordination referral, social risk screening, and PCP follow-up scheduling.

title: Claims Denial Prevention Checklist
content: Before claim submission, verify eligibility, authorization, diagnosis-procedure pairing, and modifier usage. Common denial drivers are missing documentation, absent authorization, coding mismatch, and late submission. Operational targets are denial rate below 8 percent for Medicare and below 10 percent for Commercial.

title: Care Coordination SOP
content: For eligible high-risk patients, assign care manager before discharge, complete social risk screening, schedule PCP visit within 7 days, and confirm transportation and pharmacy access. Track outreach completion in care coordination log to reduce avoidable readmissions.

title: Medication Reconciliation Policy
content: At admission, transfer, and discharge, compare home medications with orders, resolve duplicates and interactions, verify allergies, provide an updated medication list, and perform teach-back counseling. Completion target is >= 95 percent of discharges.
